claims.text: Corrosion-related degradation or retention of protection in Q235 steel is influenced by the formation and stability of a surface passive layer.
The presence of certain elements affects passive-layer formation or stability in Q235 steel.
The microstructure of Q235 steel affects passive-layer formation or stability.
Aggressive-salt exposure at 700–900 °C is the proposed intervention.
Elemental dissolution is a proposed mechanism during salt exposure.
Precipitation is a proposed mechanism during high-temperature exposure.
High-temperature salt exposure can produce microstructural changes.
The proposed intervention and mechanism will improve Q235 steel's corrosion resistance.
The proposed intervention and mechanism will improve Q235 steel's thermal stability.
The hypothesis is bounded to 700–900 °C and an exposure duration of 1000 hours.
The exact roles of individual elements and microstructural features remain uncertain.
A controlled test should vary salt-exposure temperature and duration and measure corrosion rate, microstructure, and elemental composition.
A significant increase in corrosion rate with increasing temperature and exposure time would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The stated conditions include both room- and high-temperature regimes, but the boundary and intervention cover only 700–900 °C, so no room-temperature regime is actually specified.
The hypothesis is framed to explain either degradation or retention of protection, whereas the predicted outcome states only improved corrosion resistance and thermal stability.

Increasing corrosion with temperature and time could be consistent with passive-layer instability and corrosion-related degradation, so treating that observation as falsifying is inconsistent with the stated hypothesis.

The baseline is unexposed Q235 steel, which does not provide a directly comparable corrosion-rate control under the same environment; the design also does not specify the required room-temperature or alternative-surface-state reference.
